names.name: SThree
names.event: Rule 2.6(a) deadline — Circle8 must announce a firm offer or walk away
names.close: On Circle8's Rule 2.7 firm offer or Rule 2.8 walk-away — 5pm on 7 Oct at the latest, earlier if it walks.

down.w: Undisturbed price, implied by the 15% jump to 317p on 9 Sep

up.w: Offer-period high, set on the approach

names.about: Glasgow-founded STEM recruitment specialist placing contract and permanent staff in technology, engineering and life sciences across the UK, Germany, the Netherlands and the US. FTSE 250 until the cycle turned; revenue has been falling with the contract market. Approached on 9 Sep 2026 by Circle8 Group, a $43m Nasdaq-listed IT recruiter.
names.implied: At 297.5p the market prices something close to a coin flip on a firm offer — not a done deal. The asymmetry sits in the bidder: Circle8 is a $42.7m Nasdaq company proposing an all-cash acquisition of a £361m target, financed without issuing stock, with its own shares at $0.47 and down 38% over a year.
names.setup: Unsolicited, preliminary and highly conditional approach on 9 Sep. The board rejected it unanimously on 11 Sep as significantly undervaluing the company. A Q3 trading update is due inside the offer period on 22 Sep.
names.bull: A financed Rule 2.7 announcement before the deadline, or the approach flushes out a credible trade or PE bidder in a market where 50-plus UK companies have been bid for this year.
names.bear: No cash confirmation. Rule 2.7 requires the financial adviser to confirm funds are available in full; the bidder is roughly a tenth of the target's size. It walks, Rule 2.8 locks it out for six months, and the premium unwinds.
names.kill: Any Rule 2.8 statement of no intention to bid. Or a Panel-consented extension with still no evidence of committed financing — an extension without a funding update reads bearish, not bullish.
names.angle: Cash confirmation is the binding constraint, not board willingness. That distinction is the whole trade here and takes thirty seconds to explain.

names.name: Inovio Pharmaceuticals
names.event: PDUFA target action date — INO-3107 for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
names.close: On the FDA decision, 30 Oct. Whichever way it goes, the position is over that day.

down.w: 52-week low — where it traded before the run-in; the CRL case

up.w: 52-week high, reached earlier in the review cycle

names.about: Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania DNA-medicines company with a two-decade history of clinical programmes and no approved product. Lead asset INO-3107 for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis is under FDA review via the Accelerated Approval Program. $86m market cap and a balance sheet that is itself a near-term question.
names.implied: An $86m market cap on a company whose single near-term value driver resolves in weeks. At 31% of its 52-week range the price does not embed approval — the market is discounting a company that has been here before and missed. The process markers point the other way: late-cycle review meeting complete, FDA inspections scheduled, label negotiations expected from September.
names.setup: BLA under review via the Accelerated Approval Program for RRP, a rare HPV-6/11 disease affecting an estimated 14,000 people in the US. Competitor Papzimeos (Precigen) was approved in August 2025 and already serves the indication.
names.bull: Label negotiations beginning is a meaningful late-stage signal — the agency does not usually negotiate labels on applications it intends to reject. A January 2026 position paper in The Laryngoscope recommends HPV-specific immunotherapy as preferred first-line, naming INO-3107 alongside the approved competitor.
names.bear: Inovio has a long history of missed timelines and dilution, and at $86m the balance sheet is the second binary. Papzimeos is already approved and entrenched, so approval alone doesn't guarantee commercial traction.
names.kill: Any announcement of an extension to the review period, a late-cycle inspection finding, or an equity raise before the date — a financing into a PDUFA usually says management isn't confident of a partner-funded launch.
names.angle: This is the highest-variance name on the screen and the smallest. Whatever you conclude about direction, the position-sizing answer is the interesting half: an $86m company with one decision in six weeks is where the sleeve rule earns its keep.

names.name: Capricor Therapeutics
names.event: 24-month HOPE-3 data at World Muscle Society, then PDUFA on 22 Nov
names.close: Two exits: the 24-month data at WMS (29 Sep–3 Oct) for the near event, or the PDUFA on 22 Nov if you hold through it.

down.w: 52-week low, reached after the advisory committee vote; the CRL case

up.w: 52-week high, pre-AdCom, when approval looked routine

names.about: San Diego cell-therapy company whose lead product, deramiocel, is a cardiosphere-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. BLA under review after a July advisory committee voted 9–3 against efficacy; the company then narrowed the proposed indication to upper-limb function. Partnered with Nippon Shinyaku for the US and Japan.
names.implied: A 13x 52-week range on one ticker. At 16% of that range the AdCom defeat is priced; the partial re-rate since reflects the extension. What looks underpriced is timing — the 24-month dataset goes in front of clinicians seven weeks before the PDUFA, while almost all the attention is on 22 November.
names.setup: The FDA moved the PDUFA from 22 Aug to 22 Nov, classifying the BLA amendment as a major amendment. The amendment asks CBER to review a refined indication focused solely on upper limb function — the primary endpoint of HOPE-3 — after a July advisory committee voted 9–3 against efficacy.
names.bull: CBER accepted the amendment citing significant unmet need in Duchenne, and the Phase 3 results were published in The Lancet after peer review. Continued separation at 24 months would make the narrowed indication harder to refuse.
names.bear: A 9–3 AdCom against efficacy is a very hard starting position. A securities class action alleges the statistical analysis plan was changed without FDA agreement before resubmission — that goes directly at the credibility of the p-values the case rests on.
names.kill: Any disclosure that the FDA has not accepted the refined upper-limb indication, or 24-month data that fails to separate on the primary endpoint.
names.angle: Two dated events, and the near one is the less-watched one. Knowing a conference presentation can front-run a PDUFA by seven weeks is calendar awareness that reads as filing-level work rather than headline-level.

names.name: Harworth Group
names.event: Acceptance deadline on Peel's 177.5p Rule 9 mandatory offer
names.close: On Peel's final acceptance deadline, 1pm on 25 Oct — or earlier if Peel declares the offer final under Rule 32.2.

down.w: Pre-bid close on 5 Aug, before the offer period

up.w: EPRA NDV at 30 Jun 2026 — the board's own asset value

names.about: Rotherham-based land regeneration and property developer that turns former coalfield and industrial sites in the North of England and Midlands into industrial and residential land, with a growing data-centre pipeline. Published EPRA NDV of 214.8p at June 2026. Subject of a hostile Rule 9 mandatory offer from Peel at 177.5p.
names.implied: The stock trades above the cash offer, so the market is refusing the price and pricing either a bump or the asset value. Both cases are unusually well documented: Peel points to NDV down 4.3%, a negative 1.4% total accounting return over 18 months and net finance costs up 47.6%; the board points to a 17.4% discount to NDV and a data-centre pipeline the offer ignores.
names.setup: Peel Bidco bought to exactly 30.00% on 17 Sep, forcing its voluntary offer to convert into a Rule 9 mandatory offer at the same price. The board has rejected unanimously twice and told holders to withdraw acceptances. There has been no engagement between the parties across the entire offer period.
names.bull: Peel raises to clear 50%, or the NDV argument holds and the shares re-rate as the data-centre pipeline converts — the company targets exchanging a conditional contract on one site in Q4.
names.bear: Peel sits on 30% and waits. The offer lapses with no bump, and a stock that was 143.6p in early August has no bidder and a hostile blocking stake on the register. Peel's own criticism is the bear case: one site under exclusivity may not produce cash until 2033.
names.kill: Peel declaring the offer final under Rule 32.2 — it then cannot raise. Or acceptance levels published near the deadline showing it stuck well short of 50%.
names.angle: Crossing 30% converts a voluntary offer into a mandatory one and strips every condition except acceptances. That mechanical detail changes the payoff structure, and most people discussing this stock won't know it.

ref.w: Peel's cash offer; the stock trades above it

names.name: Cogent Biosciences
names.event: PDUFA for bezuclastinib in GIST, with a second decision a month later
names.close: On the GIST decision, 30 Nov. The NonAdvSM decision on 30 Dec is a separate trade.

down.w: 52-week low, before the 152% twelve-month re-rate

up.w: 52-week high, set earlier in 2026

names.about: Waltham, Massachusetts precision-oncology company developing bezuclastinib, a selective KIT inhibitor, across gastrointestinal stromal tumours and systemic mastocytosis. Three NDAs filed or accepted, no approved product yet, $5.5bn market cap.
names.implied: Up 152% over twelve months but down 14% in the past month and 10% year to date — the market has been taking risk off into the decisions rather than adding. Three staggered PDUFAs across KIT-driven diseases means this is a sequence, not a single binary, which is why the risk score sits below the other regulatory names despite a similar setup.
names.setup: NDAs under review for bezuclastinib across three indications: GIST with a 30 Nov target date, Non-Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis on 30 Dec, and Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis newly accepted in September.
names.bull: Three shots rather than one. A GIST approval de-risks the platform ahead of the larger NonAdvSM indication a month later, and the pullback into the date has already removed some of the froth.
names.bear: A $5.5bn valuation on a company with no approved product means a lot is already assumed. A miss on the first of three would re-rate the other two at the same time.
names.kill: Any FDA communication extending a review or requesting an advisory committee — either would push the sequence past your window.
names.angle: The useful contrast with Capricor and Inovio: same regulatory structure, but staggered dates change the risk profile materially. Being able to say why is more interesting than having a view on the drug.

names.name: Precigen
names.event: Inovio's PDUFA — the read-across to the incumbent
names.close: On Inovio's decision, 30 Oct — the pair resolves on the same day.

down.w: 52-week low, before the Papzimeos commercial ramp

up.w: 52-week high — essentially where it trades

names.about: Germantown, Maryland gene-and-cell-therapy company whose Papzimeos, approved in August 2025, is the first FDA-approved treatment for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. The stock has doubled in a year on the launch. Its only near-term competitor is Inovio's INO-3107, decided on 30 Oct.
names.implied: Sitting at 95% of its 52-week range, up 104% over a year and 61% over three months, on the strength of Papzimeos being the only approved RRP therapy. That monopoly has a dated expiry risk: Inovio's decision on 30 October. The price does not appear to reflect a competitor arriving in six weeks.
names.setup: Papzimeos was approved in August 2025 as the first and only FDA-approved therapy for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. Inovio's INO-3107 targets the same indication with a simpler regimen — no additional surgery before later doses.
names.bull: Inovio gets a CRL, Papzimeos keeps the market to itself, and a crowded long stays crowded. First-mover advantage in a rare disease with an established prescriber base is real.
names.bear: An Inovio approval introduces a directly competing product into a 14,000-patient US market, and does so into a stock priced at the top of its range. This is the mirror of the Inovio trade and the two shouldn't both be owned.
names.kill: An Inovio approval, or Papzimeos launch metrics that show slower uptake than the re-rate implies.
names.angle: A genuine pair. One decision on one day moves two listed companies in opposite directions, and the smaller one is priced for failure while the larger is priced for continued monopoly. That's a cleaner way to express a view on the FDA than owning either outright.

names.name: Eleco
names.event: Court-sanctioned scheme on Accel-KKR's 235p cash offer
names.close: At scheme completion, or on any break. There is no earlier catalyst — this is the control case.

down.w: Pre-bid level, before the 70% single-day move

up.w: Accel-KKR's recommended cash offer

names.about: AIM-listed construction and engineering software group (Asta, Veeuze, Elecosoft) with subscription revenue across the UK, Germany, Sweden and the US. Board-recommended 235p cash offer from Accel-KKR announced this summer; the scheme runs into 2027.
names.implied: A 2.5% gross spread to terms. Over a scheme timetable stretching into next year that is a thin annualised return, and the market is telling you completion risk is low but not zero. The asymmetry is poor in the classic arb shape: small premium, large break risk back toward 135p.
names.setup: Board-recommended all-cash offer from Accel-KKR at 235p, valuing the equity at about £207.6m. Shares rose 70% on the announcement. The process now runs through scheme documentation, a shareholder vote and court sanction.
names.bull: A recommended cash offer from an established software buyer with no obvious competition or regulatory obstacle. Spreads on clean UK schemes usually grind in as the court date approaches.
names.bear: On an AIM line trading 191k shares a day, getting size on is slow and getting out on a break is slower. Two and a half percent does not pay for that.
names.kill: Any condition being invoked, a financing wobble, or the court date slipping materially past the guided window.
names.angle: Worth having on the screen precisely because it scores badly. It's the control case: a near-certain outcome with almost no payoff, which is what most of the merger-arb universe looks like once you price the liquidity.

names.name: Spire Healthcare
names.event: Toscafund-led 250p offer, under a Takeover Panel restriction
names.close: On a Rule 2.7 firm offer or a Rule 2.8 walk. Each PUSU extension is the marker to re-check.

down.w: 52-week low — the no-deal case

up.w: Toscafund consortium's 250p proposal

names.about: Britain's largest independent private hospital group — 39 hospitals and clinics, growing NHS and self-pay volumes, £1.5bn of revenue. In an offer period since May with a 250p proposal from a Toscafund-led consortium that has needed repeated deadline extensions and is now under a Takeover Panel restriction.
names.implied: A 1.8% spread, with the deadline extended repeatedly since June. The unusual feature is the sanction: a concert party sold 5.57% of the company without Panel consent and without 24 hours' notice, and the Panel ruled that neither Bidco nor its concert parties may acquire further shares, and that Bidco may not revise its offer except in exceptional circumstances with prior consent.
names.setup: Tulip UK Bidco, owned by funds managed by Toscafund, THCP and Ares, offering 250p. Due diligence completed; the put-up-or-shut-up deadline has been extended several times through the summer on financing.
names.bull: Due diligence is done and financing was described as near-final. A completed deal pays the spread from here.
names.bear: A bidder that has needed four extensions to finalise financing, now barred from improving its price without Panel consent. If it walks, the reference is a stock that traded at 140.8p within the year.
names.kill: A Rule 2.8 statement, or another extension without a financing confirmation.
names.angle: The Panel sanction is the detail worth knowing. A bidder that can't revise its offer has lost its main tool for getting a deal done, which is why the spread hasn't closed further despite completed diligence.

names.name: Vaxcyte
names.event: VAX-31 adult Phase 3 OPUS-1 topline safety and immunogenicity
names.close: On the OPUS-1 topline press release, guided for by the end of October.

down.w: 52-week low — the failed-readout reference

up.w: 52-week high, set on the run into the readout

names.about: San Carlos, California vaccine company developing VAX-31, a 31-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine intended to beat Prevnar 20 and Capvaxive on coverage. No approved product; $8.5bn market cap rests on a three-trial adult Phase 3 programme that is fully enrolled.
names.implied: An $8.5bn valuation on a company with no approved product, 82% of the way up its range and 81% higher over a year. This is a binary priced for success — the mirror image of Capricor. The question isn't direction, it's what's left on the upside if the trial does exactly what everyone expects.
names.setup: Guidance narrowed on 3 Sep from Q4 to 'by the end of October'. OPUS-1 is the pivotal non-inferiority trial in a three-study adult programme with 6,191 adults dosed, roughly 3,500 on VAX-31, designed in consultation with the FDA.
names.bull: A fully enrolled 6,191-patient programme with a large safety database and an FDA-aligned design. OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 follow in H1 2027, so a clean OPUS-1 de-risks a sequence rather than a single print.
names.bear: Priced near highs, so even a clean hit can be sold. A miss on any single serotype's immunogenicity in a 31-valent construct re-rates the whole platform, not just this trial.
names.kill: Guidance slipping back from 'end of October' to Q4. A schedule slip on a fully enrolled, fully dosed trial is information in itself.
names.angle: Put beside Capricor this answers 'how do you think about risk?' cleanly: two binaries, one at 16% of its range and one at 82%, same ten-week window. The trade is the gap between the odds and the price, not the science.

names.name: Moderna
names.event: Full intismeran autogene dataset, with a Phase 3 melanoma interim in H2
names.close: On the ESMO presentation, 23–27 Oct.

down.w: 52-week low — where this run started

up.w: 52-week high, set this month

names.about: Cambridge, Massachusetts mRNA platform company whose COVID and RSV vaccines fund a large oncology and rare-disease pipeline. The stock is up more than 400% this year on the intismeran autogene personalised cancer vaccine, partnered with Merck, ahead of the full dataset at ESMO in October.
names.implied: Up 427% year to date and 147% in a single month into a dated conference. Whatever intismeran autogene is worth, a very large amount of it is now in the price. This scores near zero on uncrowdedness for a reason — the interesting expression of a positive view was three months ago, and what's left is a stock that has to deliver to hold its level.
names.setup: The full dataset for the personalised cancer vaccine developed with Merck is expected at ESMO in Madrid, 23–27 October. Management expects the Phase 3 adjuvant melanoma interim analysis in H2 2026, and dedicated commercial manufacturing is already being built in Massachusetts.
names.bull: A positive interim could unlock estimate revisions across both partners' oncology franchises, and the manufacturing build signals internal confidence.
names.bear: After a 5x move, a good result is the base case and anything short of excellent is a sell. Note the quoted spread on this line is wide despite the size — $147.40 bid against $163.96 ask at the time of the snapshot.
names.kill: The Phase 3 interim slipping out of 2026, or ESMO data that is presented without the adjuvant melanoma readout attached.
names.angle: The most useful name here for demonstrating discipline: correctly identifying something as a great business and a bad entry is a more convincing answer than another bullish pitch.

names.name: Invivyd
names.when: Later in Q3 2026 (guided), i.e. by 30 Sep
names.event: DECLARATION pivotal Phase 3 topline for VYD2311 — COVID-19 prophylaxis in vulnerable adults
names.close: On the DECLARATION topline, guided for later in Q3 — by 30 Sep.

down.w: 52-week low, set this summer — the failed-trial reference

up.w: 52-week high, before the Pemgarda revenue disappointment

names.about: Waltham, Massachusetts antibody developer (formerly Adagio). One commercial product, Pemgarda, a COVID-19 pre-exposure antibody under EUA, and one pivotal programme, VYD2311, a next-generation monoclonal designed to support a BLA. $218m market cap, down 70% year to date, trading below $1.
names.implied: At 8% of its range and a $218m market cap, the price embeds a failed or commercially irrelevant readout. The trial was upsized in April after a blinded sample-size re-estimation and fully enrolled in June, so the event is real and near. Whatever the science, a sub-$1 stock into a pivotal readout is a lottery ticket with a listing-compliance clock attached.
names.setup: DECLARATION is a placebo-controlled pivotal study of VYD2311 designed to support a BLA. Topline guided to 'later in Q3 2026'. A second Phase 3, LIBERTY, comparing the antibody with an mRNA vaccine on safety and immunology, reads out on the same schedule.
names.bull: A clean efficacy hit on a fully enrolled, upsized trial with an FDA-agreed BLA path. The 52-week high is 4x the current price and the prior product already has an EUA, so the commercial channel exists.
names.bear: COVID prophylaxis demand has collapsed, the company has burned through most of its cash and the Nasdaq $1 minimum bid rule is in play. A win may be sold into if the market decides the addressable market is too small to fund a launch.
names.kill: Any further slip in the DECLARATION timeline past Q3, a reverse split announcement before the data, or a financing announced ahead of the readout.
names.angle: The purest example on this screen of why position sizing is the answer rather than the view. A name that can go to zero or 4x inside two weeks belongs at a size where either outcome is survivable — say why that number is what it is.

names.name: Savara
names.event: PDUFA target action date — MOLBREEVI in autoimmune PAP
names.close: On the FDA decision, 22 Nov. The UK MHRA decision in Q4 is an earlier tell worth watching.

down.w: 52-week low — the CRL case

up.w: 52-week high, set on the BLA acceptance

names.about: Austin, Texas rare-respiratory biotech with one asset: MOLBREEVI (inhaled molgramostim) for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, a disease with no approved therapy. BLA under review in the US, MAAs under review at the EMA and MHRA. ~$173m cash at June plus up to ~$150m of non-dilutive capital that triggers on FDA approval.
names.implied: A stock that has gone nowhere for three months into a hard-dated decision on its only asset. The market is neither pricing approval nor a rejection — it has simply stopped looking. That is the uncrowded shape this screen is built to find; the price gives you the payoff structure without a premium for attention.
names.setup: The BLA for MOLBREEVI was accepted with a PDUFA date of 22 Nov 2026. The Phase 3 IMPALA-2 data were positive on lung function and quality of life, with long-term extension data presented at ATS. UK MHRA decision expected in Q4 2026, EMA in Q1 2027.
names.bull: First-and-only therapy in an orphan indication with a clean Phase 3, no advisory committee flagged, and a balance sheet that improves by up to $150m on approval. The MHRA decision may land inside the same window and would be a leading indicator.
names.bear: A single asset, a single decision, and an inhaled biologic with manufacturing and device components that have tripped up other applicants. The flat price could also mean the market has quietly concluded the launch economics are thin.
names.kill: Any FDA request for additional data or a major-amendment extension, an advisory committee being called, or an MHRA rejection ahead of the US date.
names.angle: The MHRA-before-FDA sequencing is the point worth making: a UK decision on the same dossier due in Q4 gives an observable signal before the binary, and most US-focused holders are not watching it.

names.name: Summit Therapeutics
names.event: PDUFA target action date — ivonescimab BLA in EGFR-mutant NSCLC after a third-generation TKI
names.close: On the FDA decision, 14 Nov. A HARMONi-3 PFS readout before then is a second exit point.

down.w: 52-week low, set on the HARMONi overall-survival miss in 2025

up.w: 52-week high, set on the first HARMONi-2 read-across

names.about: Miami-based oncology company built around ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody licensed from Akeso for the US, Europe and Japan. No approved product in its territories; ivonescimab is approved and selling in China. Chaired by Bob Duggan, who owns a majority of the equity, which limits the free float.
names.implied: A $14bn company priced at a third of its range, up 37% in a month on Akeso's HARMONi-2 survival data from China. The BLA under review rests on HARMONi, where PFS was significant but OS missed at p=0.057 in April 2025; the updated OS presented at WCLC on 15 Sep showed the western-patient result converging with the global one. The price now discounts a reasonable chance of approval on PFS but not a certainty.
names.setup: BLA accepted with a PDUFA date of 14 Nov 2026 for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated non-squamous NSCLC after progression on a third-generation EGFR TKI. HARMONi-3, the larger first-line squamous study, has a PFS readout guided for H2 2026, which may fall inside the same window.
names.bull: PFS was the co-primary endpoint and was met; the OS trend is now consistent across regions with longer follow-up. A first US approval de-risks a platform that is already commercial in China and opens a much larger first-line opportunity behind it.
names.bear: An OS miss on the pivotal trial is exactly the kind of thing a conservative FDA cycle refuses on. The stock has already re-rated on somebody else's data, and a majority owner means the float is thinner than the market cap suggests.
names.kill: An FDA extension of the review, a request for an advisory committee, or HARMONi-3 PFS slipping into 2027 — the second event was meant to de-risk the first.
names.angle: Two dated events that can land inside the same six weeks, one regulatory and one clinical, on the same molecule. Being able to say which one the price is actually reacting to is the analysis.

names.name: Mirum Pharmaceuticals
names.event: PDUFA for zilurgisertib in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva on 26 Sep, then Phase 3 AZURE-1 topline for brelovitug in hepatitis delta by month-end
names.close: Two dates days apart: the 26 Sep PDUFA and the AZURE-1 topline by 30 Sep. Close after the second.

down.w: 52-week low, before the LIVMARLI growth re-rate

up.w: 52-week high, set earlier in 2026

names.about: Foster City, California rare-disease company with three marketed liver medicines (LIVMARLI, Cholbam, Ctexli) guiding to $680–700m of 2026 sales, and a late-stage pipeline in hepatitis delta (brelovitug) and cholestatic pruritus (volixibat). Profitable at the operating line, so the events here are additive rather than existential.
names.implied: Down 8% in a week and 12% over three months into two dated events, with a revenue base that pays the bills regardless. The market is trimming exposure rather than adding, which for a profitable company with a 27% gap to its 52-week high is the uncrowded end of the range. The price discounts neither event being large.
names.setup: Zilurgisertib's NDA in FOP has a PDUFA date of 26 Sep 2026 after positive pivotal Phase 2 PROGRESS data. AZURE-1, the first of two Phase 3 studies of brelovitug in chronic hepatitis delta, was guided by management on 16 Sep to read out 'in the next couple of weeks'; the Phase 2b portion showed 100% virologic response on weekly dosing.
names.bull: Two independent shots in one fortnight on a company whose base business grew LIVMARLI sales 46% year on year. Either a clean approval or a clean HDV readout resets the pipeline value, and the second one compounds.
names.bear: FOP is a very small market and a CRL would be read as a process failure; an HDV miss would hit the largest pipeline asset. Neither is existential, which is also why neither pays like the smaller names on this screen.
names.kill: A CRL citing anything other than a label negotiation, or an AZURE-1 readout that fails the primary virologic endpoint at week 48.
names.angle: Two-event names are where you can show you understand correlation: these outcomes are independent, so the payoff distribution is genuinely different from a single binary of the same size. Say that, and why it lowers the risk score.

names.name: Kodiak Sciences
names.event: Phase 3 DAYBREAK one-year topline — Zenkuda and KSI-501 versus aflibercept in treatment-naive wet AMD
names.close: On the DAYBREAK topline press release, guided for September.

down.w: 52-week low, before the re-rate — where a failed DAYBREAK would be argued

up.w: 52-week high, set in the summer run-up

names.about: Palo Alto retinal-disease biotech with no approved product. Lead asset Zenkuda (tarcocimab), a long-acting anti-VEGF with four completed Phase 3 trials behind it, and KSI-501, a bispecific that adds IL-6 inhibition. Three Phase 3 readouts guided between September and year-end, with DAYBREAK first.
names.implied: Up 222% over a year but down 22% in the past month into the readout — the market has been taking profits into the date rather than adding. A $2bn valuation on a company with no product gives credit for a non-inferiority win already; what is not priced is whether the durability data are good enough to change prescribing, which is the actual commercial question.
names.setup: DAYBREAK enrolled roughly 690 treatment-naive wet AMD patients across two comparisons against on-label aflibercept, with one-year primary endpoints. Management guided topline to September 2026. Zenkuda previously matched aflibercept on vision in GLOW1, GLOW2 and BEACON with extended dosing intervals.
names.bull: Four prior Phase 3 wins on the same molecule make a non-inferiority miss unlikely; the upside case is a durability result that supports six-month dosing, which no approved anti-VEGF offers. Two readouts in one press release doubles the chance of a positive headline.
names.bear: Non-inferiority alone is a passing grade in a crowded market with Eylea HD and Vabysmo, and the stock has already run on that expectation. A miss on either arm, or a safety signal on KSI-501's IL-6 component, re-rates the whole platform toward the $9 low.
names.kill: Guidance moving from September to Q4, or a topline that reports non-inferiority without the dosing-interval data alongside it.
names.angle: The distinction between 'the trial worked' and 'the drug will be used' is the whole analysis here. Non-inferiority is a regulatory threshold, not a commercial one, and the price has to clear the second.

names.name: BridgeBio Pharma
names.event: PDUFA target action date — BBP-418 in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (priority review)
names.close: On the FDA decision, 27 Nov.

down.w: 52-week low, before Attruby launch traction

up.w: 52-week high, set on Attruby launch momentum

names.about: Palo Alto genetic-disease company with one commercial product, Attruby (acoramidis) for ATTR cardiomyopathy, approved in the US, EU, Japan and UK, and a sequence of late-stage rare-disease filings behind it. Roughly 1,000 staff and a $13bn market cap; the events are a pipeline sequence, not a single bet.
names.implied: Down 19% in a month and 12% year to date on a company whose lead product is launched and growing, with a priority-review PDUFA ten weeks out. The price is reacting to sector flows and a Q2 guidance debate, not to the LGMD decision, which means the decision is close to free at the current level.
names.setup: BBP-418 NDA accepted with priority review and a PDUFA date of 27 Nov 2026 for LGMD2I/R9, a disease with no approved therapy. Encaleret in ADH1 follows on 8 May 2027, and infigratinib in achondroplasia is awaiting a filing decision. Attruby sales are the base under all of it.
names.bull: Priority review on an orphan indication with no competition, from a company that has now been through the FDA process successfully with acoramidis. Three staggered decisions inside nine months means the risk is spread rather than concentrated.
names.bear: Rare-disease launches are slow and a $13bn valuation already assumes several of them. LGMD2I is small; approval alone will not move a stock this size much, so the asymmetry is modest by construction.
names.kill: A review extension or an advisory committee for BBP-418, or a change in the encaleret PDUFA date — both would suggest the FDA relationship has cooled.
names.angle: The useful pairing with Capricor and Savara: same event type, wildly different risk scores, and the difference is entirely in single-point-of-failure and downside. Being able to decompose the risk score is more convincing than a view on the drug.

names.name: Egetis Therapeutics
names.event: PDUFA target action date — Emcitate (tiratricol) NDA in MCT8 deficiency
names.close: On the FDA decision, 28 Sep.

down.w: 52-week low, before the NDA acceptance — the CRL case

up.w: 52-week high, set this month into the date

names.about: Stockholm-listed orphan-drug company. Emcitate (tiratricol) is the first and only approved treatment for MCT8 deficiency in the EU, launched in Germany in May 2025, with Q2 sales of SEK 17m. US NDA under priority review; a US launch, a rare-disease priority review voucher sale and a European rollout are the whole investment case. 56 staff.
names.implied: Up 50% in three months to 92% of its range ten days before the decision. The market has priced approval; the late-cycle meeting and label negotiations that management referenced on 16 Sep are consistent with that. What is left is the difference between an approval and an approval-plus-voucher, against a 54% drop to the low if the agency surprises.
names.setup: NDA accepted with priority review in March; PDUFA date 28 Sep 2026. FDA confirmed it expects to complete the review on time and does not plan an advisory committee. Management said on 16 Sep that label negotiations are under way. A SEK 350m placing in June funds the US launch.
names.bull: EU-approved drug, clean review process by every observable marker, no AdCom, and a priority review voucher on approval that is worth a large fraction of the market cap. Product availability in the US 8–12 weeks after the date.
names.bear: At 92% of range there is very little left on the upside reference, and a CRL on a small Swedish company would be brutal for liquidity. Even a clean approval can be sold on the news given the run.
names.kill: Any announcement of an extended review or a request for additional data before 28 Sep, or a delay to the guided US product availability window after approval.
names.angle: The mirror of Savara: identical event type, opposite crowding. Putting these two next to each other is a cleaner way to talk about 'what's priced in' than any single-name pitch.

names.name: PolyPid
names.event: PDUFA target action date — D-PLEX100 NDA in abdominal colorectal surgery (priority review)
names.close: On the FDA decision, 28 Nov.

down.w: 52-week low, before the SHIELD II data and the Azurity deal

up.w: 52-week high, set on the NDA acceptance

names.about: Petah Tikva, Israel drug-delivery company. D-PLEX100 is a polymer-lipid matrix placed in the surgical wound that releases antibiotic locally for weeks, aimed at preventing surgical site infection after colorectal surgery. NDA under priority review; US and Canada commercial rights licensed to Azurity in July for $30m of upfront and near-term milestones. $99m market cap.
names.implied: A $99m company with a priority-review PDUFA that the FDA accepted one quarter ahead of the company's own guidance with no filing issues. At 80% of range the market has moved toward approval but the absolute size means the reference levels understate the move: the 52-week high is only 10% above the price, which tells you how little the stock has been allowed to discount a launch.
names.setup: NDA accepted 27 Jul 2026 with priority review and a PDUFA date of 28 Nov 2026, ahead of the Q1 2027 guidance. Acceptance triggered a $15m milestone from Azurity, completing $30m of upfront and near-term payments. EMA MAA submission planned for Q3 2026.
names.bull: Priority review, no filing issues, a commercial partner already contracted and paying, and a large addressable procedure volume. An approval converts the company from a binary into a royalty stream, which is a different valuation model entirely.
names.bear: $1m a day of trading volume with a 2% quoted spread means getting size on is slow and getting out on a CRL is slower. Drug-device combinations with novel matrices draw manufacturing scrutiny, and the company has one shot.
names.kill: A review extension, a manufacturing inspection finding, or an equity raise announced before the date — with Azurity paying milestones, a raise would say the company does not expect the approval milestone to arrive on time.
names.angle: The liquidity score is the whole conversation on this one. The event is attractive; the instrument is not. Knowing when to pass on a good event because the line cannot be traded is a more senior answer than finding it.

names.name: easyJet
names.when: Scheme document by 15 Oct; Court Meeting w/c 9 Nov
names.event: Scheme document publication, then Court Meeting and General Meeting on Apollo's 715p recommended offer
names.close: Two checkpoints: the scheme document by 15 Oct (the spread should move on publication), then the Court and General Meetings in the week of 9 Nov.

down.w: Undisturbed price, back-solved from the stated 81% premium to the May 2026 level

up.w: Apollo's recommended cash offer

names.about: Luton-based low-cost airline, Europe's second largest by passengers, with around 300 aircraft and a holidays business. Agreed on 6 Aug 2026 to a recommended £5.7bn cash acquisition by Apollo funds at 715p per share, after seeing off Castlelake. Rejoins the FTSE 100 on 21 Sep, probably briefly.
names.implied: A 6.7% gross spread on a recommended, financed, board-and-founder-backed cash offer is far wider than a clean UK scheme normally trades. The market is charging for one specific thing: EU rules require an airline to be majority owned and effectively controlled by EU nationals, and Apollo is American. The scheme document was delayed to 15 Oct explicitly to keep talking to aviation regulators. The spread is the price of that structure being accepted.
names.setup: Apollo's Eagle Bidco agreed a 715p cash offer on 6 Aug with a rollover alternative; the Haji-Ioannou family (15%) has agreed to vote in favour and roll. On 25 Aug both sides extended the scheme document deadline from 3 Sep to 15 Oct to continue engagement with aviation regulators. Court Meeting and General Meeting expected in the week of 9 Nov; completion still guided by end of Q1 2027.
names.bull: Recommended cash with committed funding, the founder's block voting for it, and an 81% premium that nobody is going to vote against. If the scheme document arrives on time with the ownership structure resolved, the spread should compress sharply on publication rather than at completion.
names.bear: If the regulatory structure cannot be made to work, the reference is a stock that traded under 400p in May in a sector down double digits on fuel. Every extension without a published document widens the tail rather than narrowing it.
names.kill: A second extension to the scheme document deadline, or the document being published with a structure that requires a fresh regulatory process before completion.
names.angle: Spreads carry information. Ask why a recommended UK scheme trades at 7% when the average is under 2%, and the answer is a piece of EU aviation law — which is a better interview answer than anything about airlines.

names.name: Bodycote
names.when: Scheme document by 29 Sep; CVC to clarify by Day 53
names.event: Scheme document on Veritas's 940p recommended offer; CVC must declare whether it will counter
names.close: On CVC's decision — a counterbid or a Rule 2.8 statement. The scheme document by 29 Sep starts that clock; a named bidder must clarify by Day 53.

down.w: Undisturbed, back-solved from the 37.5% premium to the 3-month VWAP to 21 May

up.w: Offer-period high — the most the market has paid for a counterbid so far

names.about: Macclesfield, England — the world's largest heat-treatment and thermal-processing group, around 130 plants in 22 countries serving aerospace, defence, automotive and energy. After approaches from Apollo, CVC and Veritas since May, the board recommended Veritas Capital's 940p cash offer on 1 Sep 2026. CVC, which had bid 915p, says it is reviewing its position.
names.implied: The stock trades above a recommended cash offer, so the market is not pricing the deal on the table; it is pricing CVC. Three bidders have now put numbers on this company within four months, and CVC's last proposal was 915p before Veritas went to 940p. The 13.5p above terms is the market's price for CVC coming back at, say, 975p or more.
names.setup: Veritas's Vulcan Alpha Bidco announced a Rule 2.7 firm offer at 940p on 1 Sep after Bodycote ran a parallel process with CVC and Veritas. Apollo had withdrawn a £1.52bn proposal in June. The buyback was suspended on 2 Sep. Scheme document due within 28 days; a named competing bidder must clarify its intentions by Day 53 of the timetable.
names.bull: A genuine auction with a US aerospace-and-defence specialist as the incumbent and a large European buyout firm that has already bid once. CVC needs only to clear 940p by a margin the board can recommend.
names.bear: If CVC walks, the stock settles back to the offer and you have paid 1.4% for nothing, over a timetable to Q1 2027. A break of the Veritas deal itself is a 28% fall to the undisturbed level.
names.kill: A CVC statement under Rule 2.8 that it does not intend to bid, or the scheme document arriving with irrevocables from a large enough block to make a counterbid impractical.
names.angle: Trading above terms is a specific claim: the market believes the auction is not over. Say what the 13.5p premium implies about the probability-weighted counterbid and you have shown you can read a price, not just a headline.

ref.w: Veritas's recommended cash offer incl. 7.2p dividend; the stock trades above it

names.name: Gamma Communications
names.when: Scheme document by 29 Sep; Waterland's position to be clarified
names.event: Scheme document on Epiris's 1,120p recommended offer; the market is waiting on Waterland
names.close: On Waterland's decision — a counterbid or a Rule 2.8 statement. Scheme document due by 29 Sep.

down.w: Undisturbed close on 7 Apr 2026, before the offer period

up.w: Offer-period high — where the market went when a Waterland break-up bid looked live

names.about: Newbury, England cloud communications provider — hosted voice, SIP trunking, connectivity and collaboration software sold mostly through channel partners across the UK and Europe. H1 2026 revenue £330m, net debt near zero. Recommended a £1.02bn cash offer from Epiris at 1,120p on 1 Sep 2026, days after confirming talks with Waterland, which had planned a break-up with Giacom.
names.implied: A stock a few pence above a recommended cash offer, having touched 1,207p in the offer period. The 52-week high is the more interesting number: the market was prepared to pay 8% above the eventual offer at one point, when a Waterland–Giacom break-up bid looked live. That premium has mostly left the price, which says the market now doubts a counter, without being sure.
names.setup: Epiris's Bradbury Bidco announced a Rule 2.7 firm offer at 1,120p on 1 Sep, a 53% premium to the 732p undisturbed price and 41% to the one-month average. Directors have committed their shares. Scheme document within 28 days, shareholder vote at least 21 days later; completion guided for H1 2027 subject to antitrust and regulatory clearances.
names.bull: A second named bidder with a strategic partner and a stated plan. If Waterland returns with a break-up structure, the reference is the 1,207p offer-period high. If not, you hold a recommended cash offer at a 0.4% premium — a small cost for the option.
names.bear: H1 2027 completion is a long timetable to earn nothing, and an FTSE 250 telecoms deal has both CMA and Ofcom-adjacent clearance risk. A break takes the stock toward 732p.
names.kill: A Rule 2.8 no-intention statement from Waterland, or the scheme document showing irrevocables that lock out a counterbid.
names.angle: Compare with Bodycote: two UK schemes, both trading above terms, one with a counterbidder that has already bid once (CVC) and one with a counterbidder that only ever talked (Waterland). The difference in premium above terms — 1.4% versus 0.4% — is the market grading the two counterbids. Explain that.

ref.w: Epiris's recommended cash offer; the stock trades just above it

names.name: Capricorn Energy
names.event: DNO scheme document; Genel's rival scheme has not formally lapsed
names.close: On Genel's response to DNO's scheme document (due by 29 Sep) — a raise, or a formal withdrawal.

down.w: Undisturbed close on 10 Mar 2026, before the offer period

up.w: DNO's $5.214 all-cash offer, converted at today's rate (sterling election available)

names.about: Edinburgh-based oil and gas producer, formerly Cairn Energy, whose remaining core asset is a producing position in Egypt's Western Desert. Agreed in July to be bought by Genel Energy at $4.74 a share, then switched its recommendation to DNO's $5.214 cash offer on 1 Sep 2026. DNO amended the terms to all-cash on 17 Sep. 41 employees.
names.implied: A 1.6% spread to a recommended, cash-funded offer from a bidder with the money on its balance sheet, in a situation that has already been contested once. The market treats Genel's $4.74 scheme as dead but not buried — Capricorn said it does not currently intend to ask the court to sanction it, which is not the same as lapsing. The spread is mostly Egyptian government approval and a small currency term.
names.setup: Genel agreed a $4.74 deal in July. DNO's Bidco announced a recommended $5.214 offer on 1 Sep — originally $4.224 cash plus a $0.99 special dividend — and on 17 Sep restructured it to $5.214 entirely in cash so payment no longer depends on Capricorn declaring the dividend. Scheme document by 29 Sep; completion targeted for Q4 2026 or Q1 2027, subject to Egyptian approvals.
names.bull: Cash from existing resources, a bidder that wants Egypt as a third core region and has just shown it will improve terms for certainty. Genel, having been snubbed by DNO in its own approach, has both motive and a live scheme to come back with.
names.bear: A £262m oil company with 176k shares a day: the spread is thin and the exit on a break is not. Egyptian approvals are the kind of condition that slips quietly.
names.kill: Genel formally withdrawing, which removes the only source of upside above 388p, or DNO's scheme document disclosing a regulatory condition with no timetable.
names.angle: The all-cash amendment is the detail: DNO removed dividend-execution risk from its own offer to make it cleaner than a rival's. That is a bidder behaving like it expects a fight, and it is the kind of thing an interviewer wants to hear you noticed.

ref.w: Genel's earlier $4.74 agreed offer — not formally lapsed

names.name: Sturm, Ruger & Co.
names.event: Beretta partial tender offer for ~15% of the shares at $44.80 expires
names.close: On the tender expiry (11.59pm New York, 15 Oct) and the proration result published after it.

down.w: Pre-tender close on 16 Sep, back-solved from the stated 21% premium

up.w: Beretta's tender price — for up to 2.4m shares only, so tenders are prorated

names.about: Southport, Connecticut firearms manufacturer — Ruger and Marlin rifles, pistols and revolvers, plus a castings business — with no debt and a long dividend history. Beretta Holding of Luxembourg flagged interest in March and on 17 Sep 2026 launched a partial cash tender for up to 2,400,184 shares at $44.80. Existing shareholders keep the rest of their position.
names.implied: A partial tender is a different instrument from a takeover: the $44.80 is real, but only for the fraction of your shares that gets accepted. If every holder tenders, roughly one share in seven is taken at $44.80 and the rest stay in a stock that was $37 a fortnight ago. The price at $40.29 is the blend — the market is pricing a moderate acceptance rate plus a strategic holder arriving on the register.
names.setup: Beretta Holding commenced the tender on 17 Sep at $44.80, a 21% premium to the prior close and 20% to the 60-day VWAP before its March announcement. No financing condition and no minimum tender condition. Expires one minute after 11.59pm New York time on 15 Oct unless extended.
names.bull: A strategic buyer with no conditions paying a 21% premium for a block, which usually precedes either a larger approach or a long-term anchor holding. Low acceptance rates by retail holders mean institutional tenders get less prorated than the arithmetic suggests.
names.bear: After the tender closes, a 15% holder with board ambitions and a stock that has to find its own level again. The $44.80 applies to at most a fraction of the position, so the blended upside is well below the headline.
names.kill: Beretta amending or withdrawing the tender before expiry, or a preliminary acceptance count so high that proration makes the effective price close to the pre-tender level.
names.angle: Proration arithmetic is a good five-minute problem: what is the expected blended exit price at a 60%, 80% and 100% tender rate, and at what current price does the trade stop paying? That is more useful than a view on firearms demand.

names.name: Reliance Worldwide
names.event: End of the unusual 'go-shop' window in which the board may solicit a superior proposal to Brookfield's
names.close: On 16 Oct when the go-shop closes — a superior proposal is on the table by then, or it isn't.

down.w: Pre-approach level, back-solved from the stated 43% premium to the six-month VWAP

up.w: Brookfield's US$3.38 cash offer, converted at today's AUD rate — it floats

names.about: ASX-listed, Atlanta-run plumbing products group behind SharkBite push-to-connect fittings, John Guest, Cash Acme and Holman. Most profit comes from North America, where tariffs and lower volumes cut adjusted operating profit by over 11% in FY26. Agreed on 16 Sep 2026 to a Brookfield scheme at US$3.38 a share after four approaches since April.
names.implied: About 3.5% below an offer denominated in US dollars, on a timetable to Q1 2027, with a go-shop that ends on 16 Oct. The spread is the market's blend of currency risk, scheme execution and a small probability that the go-shop produces a rival. Brookfield holds matching rights, which caps how much a rival can win by and therefore how much the go-shop is worth.
names.setup: Brookfield Capital Partners made proposals at A$4.15, A$4.25 and A$4.50 before a fourth in August at US$3.38 (A$4.75 at the time). Scheme implementation deed signed 16 Sep with a go-shop to 16 Oct, a US$25.3m break fee and a reverse break fee on the same terms. Shareholder vote and court approval to follow; completion guided for Q1 2027.
names.bull: A go-shop is rare in Australian deals and signals the board thinks a higher bid is possible; the break fee is modest and the asset is a global brand with a strategic buyer universe. Any rival has to be public by 16 Oct, which makes the option dated.
names.bear: Matching rights mean Brookfield can neutralise most rivals, and a US-dollar price on an ASX line means an AUD rally quietly erodes the offer. Below the offer on a break is the pre-approach level, 28% down.
names.kill: 16 Oct passing with no superior proposal announced, or the independent expert declining to conclude the scheme is in shareholders' best interests.
names.angle: The offer is in dollars and the shares are in Australia: the exit price moves every day without anything happening to the deal. Pointing out that a merger-arb spread here has an FX leg is the sort of second-order thing that reads as real work.

names.name: NCR Atleos
names.event: UK CMA Phase 1 decision on the Brink's acquisition — clearance, or a reference to Phase 2
names.close: On the CMA Phase 1 decision, 22 Oct.

down.w: Pre-announcement level on 25 Feb 2026, back-solved from the stated 24% premium

up.w: Brink's consideration: $30 cash + 0.1574 Brink's shares at today's price

names.about: Atlanta-based ATM manufacturer, operator and services company spun out of NCR in 2023, including the Allpoint surcharge-free ATM network. Agreed in February 2026 to be acquired by Brink's for $30 cash plus 0.1574 Brink's shares per NATL share, about $6.6bn including debt. Shareholders of both companies approved on 30 Jun; US, Brazil and India clearances are in hand.
names.implied: A 2.2% spread with one regulatory gate left that has a date on it. The CMA opened Phase 1 on 26 Aug and must decide by 22 Oct; both companies have UK cash-handling and ATM businesses, so a remedy discussion is plausible even if a Phase 2 reference is not. The stock leg of the consideration means the spread has been drifting with Brink's, which is down 4% in five days.
names.setup: Brink's agreed to buy NCR Atleos on 26 Feb 2026 for $30 cash and 0.1574 Brink's shares per share, funded with cash and a $4.5bn Morgan Stanley bridge. Shareholder approvals were obtained 30 Jun; HSR, Brazil and India have cleared. The CMA's Phase 1 deadline is 22 Oct; completion is guided for early Q1 2027.
names.bull: Every other approval is done, the deal is strategically obvious and a Phase 1 clearance — or undertakings in lieu — on 22 Oct removes the last gate. The spread should close toward the cost of carry on the day.
names.bear: A Phase 2 reference adds six months and a real chance of UK remedies; at that point the spread widens rather than closes, and the stock leg means you are also long Brink's through a period when it is guiding on synergies it has not delivered.
names.kill: A Phase 2 reference on 22 Oct, or Brink's shares falling enough that the consideration drops below the current NATL price — which turns the trade into a bet on the acquirer.
names.angle: Mixed consideration means the 'exit price' is a formula, not a number. Being able to say 'the deal is worth $46.67 today and here is the sensitivity to Brink's' is the difference between reading a press release and pricing a trade.

watch.note: Priority review decision. Roche is the wrong size to trade on it; the read-across to TED competitors is the angle.

watch.note: Priority review following a voucher. Large-cap, single-product-line impact.

watch.note: A rare-disease decision on a $7bn company; the label matters more than the stock move.

watch.note: No financing condition, no minimum. The spread is too thin to score; it is here as the arb control case alongside Eleco.

watch.note: 86.4% accepted against a 90% condition. No timestamped price this run, so dated rather than scored; the only question is whether the last 3.6% arrives.
